questions.question: Which of these CI findings should I turn into work? (Report-only so far, nothing changed.)

options.label: Shallow base fetch in setup
options.description: Replace fetch-depth: 0 in `setup` with a depth-1 fetch of the base SHA. Removes about 25 s from the critical path of every CI run.

options.label: Fast hatch env for lint/docs
options.description: Build .venv with uv before `uvx hatch run`, or re-check whether the BK-269 bug still exists. Saves about 70–100 s in each of lint and docs.

options.label: Slim the uv cache
options.description: One cache key per Python, one leg saves it, glob limited to the root pyproject.toml. Cuts about 17 cache entries to about 8 and protects the image cache from eviction.

options.label: Refresh shard durations
options.description: Rebalance .test_durations_pass1, since the test-primary shards run 180 s vs 121 s. Saves about 30 s of wall time.

options.description: I subscribe and tell you what failed or what reviewers asked, but push nothing without your go.

options.label: Don't watch
options.description: No subscription. You drive the PR yourself, e.g. with /rvw-pr and /fix-pr.

The 3.13 uv cache key embeds the runner's patch version, so the saver (3.13.16 image) and its readers (3.13.15 image) can miss each other. How should I handle it?

options.label: Fix now as a BUG item (Recommended)
options.description: New branch from master and a BUG-307 item. Set `python-version:` on the 6 uv-dev setup-uv steps and the 2 cross-platform ones, and extend the guard test so every cached setup-uv step pins it. Then a PR. This costs one more cold cache run.

options.label: File BUG-307 only
options.description: Record the diagnosis as an open item in § 7 and fix it later. Readers keep missing whenever runner images split.

options.label: Leave it
options.description: Accept the occasional misses. Images converge within days, so the keys usually match.
